[[File:Young Jedi CCG original logo.png|thumb|right|180px|Original Young Jedi logo.]]
[[File:Young Jedi Darth Maul Sith Apprentice.gif|thumb|right|200px|''Darth Maul, Sith Apprentice'' (''Menace of Darth Maul'', 1999).]]
'''Young Jedi''' is [[Decipher]]'s collectible card game based on ''Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace''. Decipher released ''Menace of Darth Maul'' on 12 May 1999 and ''Boonta Eve Podrace'' on 5 September 2001.<ref name="young-jedi-pc">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/young-jedi/ Young Jedi], Star Wars CCG Players Committee, release list. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20211005192154/https://www.starwarsccg.org/young-jedi/ Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="young-jedi-boonta">[https://www.rebelscum.com/story/front/Decipher_Presents_The_Latest_Young_Jedi_CCG_Expansion_Boonta_Eve_Podrace_5973.asp Decipher Presents the Latest Young Jedi CCG Expansion: Boonta Eve Podrace], Decipher announcement, 15 August 2001, reproduced by Rebelscum. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261107202144/https://www.rebelscum.com/story/front/Decipher_Presents_The_Latest_Young_Jedi_CCG_Expansion_Boonta_Eve_Podrace_5973.asp Internet Archive].</ref> It is a different game from [[Star Wars CCG]]. Decipher held both licenses; designers, Squadron Members, and the player base overlapped.

The [[Corellian Engineering Corporation (fan site)|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] GeoCities site published two Young Jedi lists next to its Classic Star Wars decks. The lists, ''Wizards!'' (Jedi) and ''All Droids All the time!'' (Sith), were both by Gold 31 ([[Alex Alcalde]]). Archived copies: [https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks/jedi1.html jedi1.html] · [https://web.archive.org/web/20011202101302/http://www.geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/decks/jedi1.html Wayback, 2 December 2001]; [https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks/sith1.html sith1.html] · [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009020148/https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks/sith1.html Wayback, 9 October 2026].

== Design ==
''Young Jedi'' was designed by [[Tom Braunlich]] and [[Rollie Tesh]], with [[Bill Martinson]] and [[Jerry Darcy]] developing it further. Decipher aimed it at 9- to 13-year-olds, and Braunlich said he had hoped for a simpler game with broader appeal than SWCCG. It kept SWCCG's destiny numbers, locations and Force depletion as the goal of the game.<ref name="rfd16">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yy8IGS_I1UI&t=100s Broadcast 16 - Radio Free Decipher (30 April, 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 2)], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 20 February 2022), at 01:40. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-yy8IGS_I1UI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 16 transcript]].</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yy8IGS_I1UI&t=205s Broadcast 16 - Radio Free Decipher (30 April, 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 2)], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 20 February 2022), at 03:25. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-yy8IGS_I1UI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 16 transcript]].</ref> In April 1999 Decipher's [[Carol Wisely]] noted that ''Young Jedi'' was the company's first game with numbered cards and rarity icons, and that its first set had 140 cards, against 324 in SWCCG's Premiere.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yy8IGS_I1UI&t=425s Broadcast 16 - Radio Free Decipher (30 April, 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 2)], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 20 February 2022), at 07:05. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-yy8IGS_I1UI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 16 transcript]].</ref>

== Sets ==
Decipher released eight Young Jedi sets between May 1999 and September 2001: ''Menace of Darth Maul'', ''The Jedi Council'', ''Battle of Naboo'', ''Enhanced Menace of Darth Maul'', ''Duel of the Fates'', ''Enhanced Battle of Naboo'', ''Young Jedi Reflections'' and ''Boonta Eve Podrace''.<ref name="cl">[http://www.decipher.com/youngjedi/cardlists/index.html Young Jedi Card Lists], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021201080954/http://www.decipher.com/youngjedi/cardlists/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

Decipher's description of ''Young Jedi Reflections'' listed 20-card packs, 18 packs per display, 14 Combo Battle cards ("two Battle Cards smashed into one"), 14 Double Impact cards (two distinct cards that play separately on one card), 12 Armed & Dangerous cards (characters with built-in weapons), 12 ''Boonta Eve Podrace'' preview cards and 60 foils of rare cards from earlier sets, 10 of them ultra-rare (R1) and 50 super-rare (R2); each pack was worth seven Young Jedi Points. The ten ultra-rare foils were Mace Windu, Jedi Speaker; Sebulba, Dangerous Podracer Pilot; Obi-Wan Kenobi, Jedi Student; Darth Sidious, Master of the Dark Side; Queen Amidala, Cunning Warrior; Darth Maul, Sith Assassin; Qui-Gon Jinn, Jedi Master; Aurra Sing, Bounty Hunter; Anakin Skywalker, Child of Prophecy; and Trade Federation Tank, Assault Division.<ref name="pcf-8354-118649">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=118649#118649 Basic Collecting Information], Artie Deco, quoting a Decipher web page he had saved, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (11 January 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618085001/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=118451 Internet Archive]</ref> A player posting as primogen wrote in 2005 that a ''Reflections'' box often held "well over 50 rares" besides the guaranteed premium cards.<ref name="pcf-7133-98155">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=98155#98155 yj rules... I question your ability to form a coherent thought did they do to this monkey game], primogen, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (27 August 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618062703/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=7133&view=next Internet Archive]</ref>

According to [[Jim Colson]], the FP1 Sebulba promotional foil was given out at DecipherCon in Virginia Beach (in 1999, as he recalled), as a sanctioned tournament prize in 2000–2001 and through distributors who bought Young Jedi product; FP2 Anakin came from a 1,000-point Young Jedi Points mail-in offer. In early 2002, at the end of the license, both foils were offered again for Young Jedi Points, at about 250 points each as he remembered it.<ref name="pcf-4066-55865">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55865#55865 YJCCG MoDM Foil Anakin Skywalker & Sebulba], Jim Colson (ShadowLeader), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (9 November 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618061526/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55391 Internet Archive]</ref> Colson also wrote that Young Jedi was printed in Japanese for two sets, ''Menace of Darth Maul'' and ''The Jedi Council'', with foils, and that the two promotional foils were printed in Japanese as well, given out as a ''GO!'' magazine insert and at tournaments. Each ''Young Jedi Reflections'' pack held one German Young Jedi card, with the same rarity spread as a booster pack; there were no German Young Jedi foils.<ref name="pcf-4066-55868">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55868#55868 What is the highest power total possible in YJ?], Jim Colson (ShadowLeader), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (9 November 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060617235032/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55868 Internet Archive]</ref>

== Organized play ==
The first Young Jedi World Championship was held at DecipherCon 1999, with 32 players advancing from four Friday qualifiers. Decipher wrote that "most have some Star Wars CCG experience". Greg Heisler won, and Matt Reed was runner-up.<ref name="wc99">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/yjworldchamp/index.html DecipherCon 1999: Young Jedi World Championship], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000124144623/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/yjworldchamp/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> The 2000 Young Jedi World Championship, won by Ian Vincent, ran at [[DecipherCon 2000]] alongside the SWCCG World Championship. [[The Outer Rim (fan site)|The Outer Rim]] published Young Jedi Deck Effect interviews in 2000, including SWCCG players [[Greg Heisler]], [[Tim Guzman]], [[Patrick Sullivan]], [[Brad Bedlion]], [[Jeffery Hall]], and [[Matthew Delaney]].<ref name="yjiv">[http://www.geocities.com/ev9d11/YoungJedi/Interviews/interviews.htm Deck Effect YJ Interviews], Young Jedi Deck Effect. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011122015220/http://www.geocities.com/ev9d11/YoungJedi/Interviews/interviews.htm Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="dc00">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/ DecipherCon 2000], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040217015645/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/ Internet Archive]</ref>

The [[Players Committee]] released Young Jedi virtual cards on 22 November 2002; they were tournament legal from 30 November 2002.<ref name="pc-nov02">[http://www.swccgpc.com/Archives/november02archives.htm November Updates], swccgpc.com (3 and 22 November 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030423221953/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/november02archives.htm Internet Archive]</ref> The Committee ran the 2002 Young Jedi World Championship at [[DecipherCon 2002]]. [[Jason Kilby|Jason Killby]] won $500 and a trophy, Jeremy Baker was 2nd ($200), Dale Hanak 3rd ($150) and Vincent Serret 4th ($150).<ref name="pc-nov02" /> Kilby's Dark Side and Light Side decklists were posted on swccgpc.com in the first days of January 2003;<ref name="pcf-489-8840">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=8840#8840 YJ World Champion], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (7 January 2003). Looking back in August 2005, primogen wrote that the Coruscant Guard and Destroyer Droid decks "were what killed the game", as almost everyone played them. He called the racing objective non-interactive and said the Light Side could win a racing game in seven turns "99.9%" of the time. The Players Committee's virtual cards, among them V-Radiant VII and the virtual objectives, were in his view "too little too late", and hard to playtest because the game was almost dead by then.<ref name="pcf-7133-98135">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=98135#98135 yj rules... I question your ability to form a coherent thought did they do to this monkey game], primogen, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (26 August 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618062703/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=7133&view=next Internet Archive]</ref>

== Design (1999 interviews) ==
Decipher product development leads [[Jerry Darcy]] and [[Bill Martinson]] discussed the game on ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' in April 1999, about five weeks before release. Darcy described it as a quicker "pickup game" than the ''Star Wars'' CCG. He said it could not be compatible with that game because ''Episode I'' lacked the Rebellion–Empire conflict and the same characters appear at very different ages.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DsqnSbxT25c&t=771s Broadcast 12 - Radio Free Decipher (02 April, 1999): Bill Martinson, Jerry Darcy on PD (Part 1)], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 20 February 2022), at 12:51. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-DsqnSbxT25c Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 12 transcript]].</ref> Martinson said the game was Warren Holland's conception, had been in development since October 1998, and was a focused battle game with a short turn sequence. He said it was planned as three 140-card sets, with a deck-building system proposed by Holland, and that a broad game could not be made before the film was released because the film's details were still changing.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XvKFYzu0P-k&t=293s Broadcast 13 - Radio Free Decipher (09 April, 1999): Bill Martinson, Jerry Darcy on PD (Part 2)], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 20 February 2022), at 04:53. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-XvKFYzu0P-k Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 13 transcript]].</ref>

== Playing online ==

[[TCGMix]] offers [https://tcgmix.com/youngjedi/ browser play], stock decks, a card archive and a tutorial that visitors can start without an account.<ref name="young-jedi-online">[https://tcgmix.com/youngjedi/ Young Jedi on TCGMix]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261107193213/https://tcgmix.com/youngjedi/ Internet Archive].</ref>
